claims.text: In legend Bran the Blessed, a giant and a king of Britain, was killed trying to conquer Ireland and asked to have the head buried beneath London's white hill as a guard against invaders. Through the seven years it took to carry it home, the head neither rotted nor lost its wit.

A second legend ties the land's safety to the ravens of the Tower, and its keepers have long made sure a few remain; during the Second World War, Nazi occultists, or perhaps rogue Technocrats, are said to have tried to reach the head.
